extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in mathematics, aesthetics, and popular-science essays
extracted.subtask_description: A popular-essay rubric listing eight axes used to recognize or describe why mathematical results, proofs or formulas are experienced as beautiful. Intended to guide readers (and writers/explainers) in what features typically produce mathematical aesthetic pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual elegance
rubrics_metrics.description: "The thrilling conceptual elegance, which often involves elements of surprise, economy, depth, relevance and power."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elegance is a broad gestalt: an idea that is conceptually neat and convincing, combining several virtues (surprise, economy, depth, relevance, power). Use examples where one concise idea explains or structures many phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity & power
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty arises when a result is "so simple, and so powerful" (Pythagoras's theorem given as an exemplar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value lies in minimal assumptions or statements that yield wide-ranging consequences; the combination of low descriptive complexity with high explanatory or applicative reach is prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpected connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Depth that "connects elements of maths that previously seemed unconnectable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results that reveal surprising links between disparate areas (e.g., number theory and geometry) are particularly beautiful because they change how we see relationships across mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Elegant brevity in expression (Euler's identity is given as an example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic value attaches to short, tightly written expressions or proofs that encapsulate a lot of content; concise notation or formulas that convey deep content are exemplary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise element
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cognitive jolt of a counterintuitive truth contributes to beauty; proofs or theorems that overturn naive expectations often elicit strong aesthetic responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical beauty triggers the same brain pleasure centres as art or music — correlated with "the medial orbito-frontal cortex" (per neuroscience studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty is not purely intellectual: it produces emotional/hedonic responses. Citing neuroscience links helps argue that mathematical beauty is felt similarly to other arts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purity & austerity
rubrics_metrics.description: Russell's "supreme beauty" — "cold and austere, like sculpture… sublimely pure."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal ornamentation, a sense of formal purity, and restraint (rather than rhetorical flourish) are aesthetic virtues; austere, sculptural forms of argument or formula are admired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquired understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty "grows as we understand more"; it requires patience and technical knowledge to be fully perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike many visual or musical beauties, mathematical beauty often depends on background knowledge and sustained engagement; evaluators should account for the role of learning and increasing appreciation over time.
